payload.summary: Two tests fail on a shallow clone as ordinary assertion failures rather than refusing, so every Claude Cloud session running npm run test sees two spurious regressions
payload.detail: Hit and diagnosed in a Claude Code remote session on 2026-09-02, while checking whether a CI failure on PR #2521 was real. The remote container clones this repository shallow (106 commits at session start), and on that clone npm run test reports 'Test Files 2 failed | 945 passed' with 12063 tests passing. Both failures are artefacts of the truncated history, not defects: tests/clinical-hazard-controls.test.ts fails with 37 entries of the form 'manifest: reviewedCommit does not exist 883f1007a85cd4e02198f39c12c4a4e467d4b89e' and 'H1: path is absent from reviewedCommit src/lib/answer-verification.ts', and tests/rag-plan-package-parity.test.ts fails with 'manifest reconciledBase is unavailable locally: f3d1a3cce2c943ad3083425ed9c7c46dbef23087' from scripts/build-rag-plan-packages.mjs --check --require-origin-main. PROVEN environmental rather than assumed: git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository returned true and git cat-file could not resolve either commit; after git fetch --deepen=3000 brought the clone to 5466 commits both commits resolved and both test files passed (Test Files 2 passed, Tests 19 passed) with no code change whatsoever. WHY IT MATTERS: this is the single broadest gate in the repository, and on the container type these sessions run in it always reports two red files. An agent reading that output has to either investigate both from scratch, as this session did, or learn to ignore failures in the full suite -- and the second habit is the dangerous one, because it is exactly how a real regression in one of these two files would be waved past. The failures also name clinical hazard controls, which is the worst possible file to train anyone to skip. THE PATTERN TO ADOPT ALREADY EXISTS in this repository: docs/outstanding-issues.md records other surfaces that detect a shallow clone and refuse explicitly rather than producing an indeterminate result, including an exported shallowCloneRefusal that prints no inventory and exits 1, and check:dead-code-candidate which refuses a shallow assessment and tells the caller to run git fetch --deepen=2000 first. NEXT STEP: have both tests check git rev-parse --is-shallow-repository, or the resolvability of the specific manifest commit, before asserting, and either skip with a named reason or fail with the deepen remediation in the message, so the output distinguishes 'cannot be assessed here' from 'this is broken'. Do not simply delete or relax the assertions -- verifying that a manifest's reviewedCommit still exists is the point of both.
payload.source: Claude Code remote session on PR #2521, 2026-09-02; reproduced and cleared by git fetch --deepen=3000
